items.title: Section: When Keeping the Scripture Genuinely Serves More Beings Than Giving It Away

items.zh: 又觀察已，若自了知，我於此法無少慳纏，亦無別意，但為成辦勝所須義不應施者，菩薩爾時應更思忖：我持此法施於彼者，為為損害自煩惱耶？為為圓滿智資糧耶？為為愛念諸眾生耶？
items.en: Having examined further, if one recognises no trace of stinginess or any other obstructing affliction at all, but genuinely should not give it because of an excellent, legitimate need, one should then further consider: in giving this teaching to that person, would I be overcoming my own affliction? Would I be completing my provisions of wisdom? Would I be expressing genuine love for beings?

items.zh: 既思忖已，便正了知，我都不見自有煩惱。見不施彼此經卷等，現法、當來我智資糧展轉增勝，非施於彼建此功德；但於當來薄饒法利，非豐覺慧。
若不施彼，便能修集利益安樂一切眾生巧方便智，即為愛念此一眾生及餘一切；若施於彼，唯成愛念此一眾生，非餘一切。菩薩如是如實知已，不施彼者，無罪、無悔；亦不違越菩薩淨戒。
items.en: If, by not giving it away, one is able to cultivate the skilful wisdom that benefits and brings peace to all beings, this is expressing genuine love for this one being and for every other being at once; if one gives it away, this expresses love only for this one being, not for all the rest. Bodhisattvas, having genuinely understood this, incur no fault and no regret in declining, and do not violate their own pure precepts.

items.title: How to Gracefully Decline — Never a Blunt Refusal

items.zh: 云何菩薩方便不施？謂諸菩薩不忍直言遣來求者，謂我不能惠施於汝。要當施設方便善巧，曉喻發遣。
items.en: How do bodhisattvas skilfully decline? Bodhisattvas cannot bear to bluntly tell a petitioner, "I cannot give this to you." They must instead find some skilful, considerate approach, gently explaining the matter so the petitioner departs at ease.

items.title: Section: Purifying Ownership — Everything Already Given to the Buddhas of the Ten Directions

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩先於所畜一切資具、一切施物為作淨故，以淨意樂，捨與十方諸佛菩薩。譬如苾芻於己衣物為作淨故，捨與親教、軌範師等。
items.en: Bodhisattvas first purify all the requisites and objects they stockpile for giving, with a genuinely pure intention giving them over to the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions. This is just as a monastic, in order to purify ownership of their own robes, gives them over to a preceptor or instructing teacher.

items.zh: 如是菩薩淨施因緣，雖復貯畜種種上妙一切資具、一切施物，猶得名為安住聖種，生無量福。常於此福多思惟故，於一切時隨逐增長。恒
items.en: Through this cause of purified giving, bodhisattvas, though they still stockpile every kind of fine requisite and object for giving, are nonetheless said to abide in the noble lineage, generating boundless merit. Because they constantly reflect on this merit, it continues to grow at every moment.

items.title: Section: Observant Giving Closes Dharma-Giving — Freely Given When Fitting, Gracefully Declined When Not

items.zh: 於一切作淨施物，如佛菩薩所寄護持，見來求者即應觀察。若隨所欲作淨施物惠施彼時，稱當正理，應作是念：諸佛菩薩無有少物於諸眾生而不施者。如是知已，取淨施物施來求者，令所願滿。
items.en: Regarding everything already purified in this way, held only as though entrusted by the buddhas and bodhisattvas for safekeeping, seeing a petitioner arrive, one carefully observes. If giving the purified object exactly as requested genuinely fits what is right, one reflects: no buddha or bodhisattva ever withholds even the smallest thing from beings. Knowing this, one takes the purified object and gives it, fully satisfying the request.

items.zh: 若觀施時，不稱正理，即應念先作淨施法。告言：賢首！如是等物是他所有，不許施汝。軟言曉喻，方便發遣。或持餘物二倍三倍，恭敬施與，然後發遣。
items.en: If giving does not fit what is right, one recalls the earlier act of purification and gently explains: good friend, this object belongs to another, and I am not permitted to give it to you — offering this in soft, considerate words. Or one gives some other object worth double or triple, respectfully, before sending the petitioner off.

items.zh: 令彼了知，菩薩於此非慳貪故，不欲施我；定當於此經卷等法不自在故，不施於我。當知是名菩薩巧慧而行法施。

items.title: Section: Giving Understood Through Four Kinds of Unobstructed Wisdom

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於一切施，謂法施、財施、無畏施。若異門、若體相、若釋名、若因果差別，如實了知而行惠施，當知亦名菩薩巧慧而行布施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, regarding every kind of giving — giving the teaching, giving material things, giving freedom from fear — truly understand its different terms, its intrinsic nature, the explanation of its name, and its distinct causes and effects, and give accordingly. This too should be understood as a bodhisattva's giving guided by skilful wisdom.

items.title: Section: Giving Shaped by the Four Immeasurable States of Mind

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，於諸有怨，以慈意樂而行惠施；於諸有苦，以悲意樂而行惠施；於諸有德，以喜意樂而行惠施；於諸有恩、親善、同意，以捨意樂而行惠施；當知亦名菩薩巧慧而行布施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, towards those who bear them ill will, give with loving-kindness; towards those who suffer, give with compassion; towards those of genuine virtue, give with shared gladness; and towards those to whom they owe kindness, or who are dear friends or of like mind, give with equanimity. This too should be understood as a bodhisattva's giving guided by skilful wisdom.

items.title: Section: Four Classic Obstacles to Giving, Named

items.zh: 又諸菩薩於其施障及彼對治如實了知。此中施障略有四種。一、先未串習，二、施物尠闕，三、耽著上妙悅意財物，四、觀見當來具足財果而深欣樂。
items.en: Bodhisattvas truly understand giving's own obstacles and how each is overcome. These obstacles are, in brief, four: first, not having habituated giving in the past; second, having genuinely little to give; third, attachment to some particularly fine and pleasing possession; fourth, deeply anticipating and delighting in the abundant wealth a future result will bring.

items.title: Section: Overcoming the Habit of Never Having Given Before

items.zh: 若諸菩薩現有種種可施財物，雖見求者正現在前，而於惠施心不趣入；菩薩爾時即以正慧速疾通達，是我於施先未串習所作過失。
items.en: If bodhisattvas, though possessing various objects that could be given, and though a petitioner genuinely stands before them, find their mind reluctant to give — they swiftly recognise, through genuine wisdom, that this reluctance is the fault of never having habituated giving in the past.

items.zh: 我於先世決定於施曾未串習，致令今世現有種種可施財物，雖見求者正現在前，而於惠施心不趣入。若於今世不強思擇而行施者，復於來世定當憎背所應行施。菩薩如是正通達已，用此施障對治為依，力勵思擇而行惠施，能不隨逐先未串習所作過失，自在而行。
items.en: I certainly failed to habituate giving in past lives, which is why this present reluctance arises now. ... If, in this present life, I do not force myself to deliberately choose to give, I will certainly come to resent and turn away from giving in future lives as well. Having genuinely recognised this, bodhisattvas rely on this very understanding as the antidote, forcefully choosing to give, and thereby no longer follow the fault of unhabituated giving, acting instead with genuine freedom.

blocks.text: How to say no without hurting, a remarkable technique of "pre-giving" everything to the Buddhas, and four obstacles to generosity.

If there is no stinginess, but keeping the scripture serves more beings (Venerable Miào Jìng: "without this book, I would be mute, unable to teach"), one keeps it: "this expresses love for this one being and every other being at once".
"Bodhisattvas cannot bear to bluntly say, 'I cannot give this to you.'" They gently explain, offering something else.

"Bodhisattvas first purify all the objects they keep for giving, with pure intention giving them over to the Buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions", "just as a monastic, to purify ownership of their robes, gives them over to a preceptor". Though they keep things, "they abide in the noble lineage". When a petitioner comes and giving is not fitting, one says truthfully: "Good friend, this object belongs to another, and I am not permitted to give it to you."

They understand giving's terms, nature, explanation, and expression. "Towards those who bear ill will, they give with loving-kindness; towards the suffering, with compassion; towards the virtuous, with shared joy; towards others, with equanimity." Venerable Miào Jìng: repaying ill will with kindness is the bodhisattva's greatness.
Not having habituated giving before; having little; attachment to a cherished object; and the wrong view of giving for future reward.
"I certainly failed to habituate giving in past lives; if I do not force myself to give now, I will certainly be the same in the future." So one gives.

quiz.q: The English renders "jí chéng chī yǎ" as "without the means to further my own understanding." How do the lectures explain it?
options: both read it literally — without the scripture one becomes dull and mute, unable to teach; the English softens it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: without this book now, I would become mute, unable to teach. Master Cháng Bǎi: in this present life, without the scripture one would become dull and mute. The English softens this strong statement.

quiz.q: If the bodhisattva has no stinginess or other affliction but withholds the scripture because of a genuine, excellent need, how does the treatise judge it?
options: a breach of the bodhisattva precepts
if by not giving one can cultivate the skilful wisdom that benefits all beings, this is love for this one and all others; declining incurs no fault or regret and does not violate the precepts
quiz.why: If not giving lets one cultivate the skilful wisdom that benefits all beings, this expresses love for this one being and all others; giving would express love for this one only. Declining "incur[s] no fault and no regret … and do[es] not violate their own pure precepts." Master Cháng Bǎi: giving it to him expresses love for only one being, not all.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas give their stockpiled requisites over to the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the ten directions, as a monastic purifies robes by giving them to a preceptor. How does Venerable Miào Jìng compare the two?
options: the bodhisattva actually sends the things away
the bodhisattva gives to the buddhas of the ten directions — the recipient differs, but the meaning is the same
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the bodhisattva's purification gives things to the buddhas of the ten directions — that is the difference, but the meaning is the same. Master Cháng Bǎi: one keeps only the right of use, not ownership.

quiz.q: Regarding giving the teaching, material giving, and giving freedom from fear, what four aspects do bodhisattvas truly understand?
options: different terms, intrinsic nature, explanation of the name, distinct causes and effects
quiz.why: "Regarding every kind of giving — giving the teaching, giving material things, giving freedom from fear — [they] truly understand its different terms, its intrinsic nature, the explanation of its name, and its distinct causes and effects."

quiz.q: "Towards those who bear them ill will, give with loving-kindness." How does Venerable Miào Jìng describe this?
options: that is repaying ill will with kindness
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: that is repaying ill will with kindness — this is the greatness of bodhisattvas, called "superior intention."

quiz.q: "Towards those to whom they owe kindness, dear friends, or those of like mind, give with equanimity." How do the two lectures explain this equanimity?
options: Cháng Bǎi: giving with equanimity means letting go of stinginess; Miào Jìng: giving with a pure mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: with an intention of equanimity, letting go of stinginess, one gives. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving with a pure mind. Neither frames it as removing favoritism.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas have objects to give and a petitioner stands before them, yet their mind is reluctant. Through genuine wisdom, what fault do they recognise?
options: never having habituated giving in the past
quiz.why: Possessing objects and with a petitioner present, yet reluctant, "they swiftly recognise, through genuine wisdom, that this reluctance is the fault of never having habituated giving in the past." Master Cháng Bǎi: no habit of giving in past lives, lacking the seeds of giving.
